page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is configured with 32 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. Multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, falls within the middle 50% average tier. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25% tier, although uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average range at 80.47 GB/sec and 48.72 GB/sec respectively. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 301.82 tokens/sec for small 135M parameter language models, while prompt processing speeds and static web serving throughput remain average.

The c2d-highcpu-16 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, owing to its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, making it unsuitable for large-scale database hosting or heavy deep learning training. It is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate-scale CPU-based inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. With 8 physical cores and a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server delivers strong single-core CPU performance and high memory scores, both ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks. Multi-core execution, software compilation, and static web serving throughput align with average tier performance. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, representing a tradeoff that prioritizes raw CPU execution over memory capacity or local disk speed. It is highly suitable for compute-bound workloads, including software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
